top.title: Where the Yankees' bullpen stands and what's next after latest addition
top.description: Rebuilding the Yankees' bullpen was an early offseason priority for GM Brian Cashman. On Monday, the Yanks agreed with veteran lefty Brent Suter on a one-year contract, as first reported by ESPN's Jeff Passan. Suter, 37, an 11-year MLB veteran, split time last season with the Los Angeles Angels and Atlanta Braves, posting a 3.36 ERA (122 ERA-plus) in 54 appearances, covering 91 innings. Earlier this month, closer David Bednar accepted the $23.15 million free agent qualifying offer, securing his services for 2027. Veteran lefty Tim Hill was re-signed and the Yanks reunited with right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga on a two-year deal, after his successful 2026 season with the Arizona Diamondbacks . Right-handers Fernando Cruz and Luis Gil were non-tendered last week, saving roughly $4.6 million in estimated 2027 salary. The expensive reunion with Bednar and the signing of Loaisiga (set to earn $18 million through 2028) and Suter (guaranteed $4 million, with an option for 2028) might be the extent of the Yanks' heavy pursuit of relievers this winter. Top free agent lefty Adrian Morejon has the Yanks' interest, but he could command a lucrative multi-year deal, while free agent righty Paul Blackburn could net a similar contract as Loaisiga received. And the Yanks have further business to address - before or after the anticipated Dec. 1 MLB lockout - including ways to upgrade or boost depth at catcher, the infield and center field. Moving third baseman Ryan McMahon's remaining $16 million contract for 2027 and exploring potential deals for Luis Garcia Jr., Ryan Weathers and the Yanks' pitching surplus are also up for discussion. Suter gives the Yankees three lefties in their 2027 bullpen, along with Hill and Brent Headrick, a converted starter who had a breakout 2026 season but tired down the stretch. The soft-tossing Suter brings a wealth of bullpen experience and a knack for inducing soft contact and groundballs, which he did at a roughly 50-percent clip in 2026, per MLB Statcast. Armed with a sinker-changeup-fastball-slider mix, Suter has generally produced neutral splits; he was better against righty hitters in '26, limiting them to a .651 OPS versus .772 against lefty hitters. A 31st-round draft pick by the Milwaukee Brewers in 2012, Suter is a Harvard graduate who received his degree in environmental science and public policy. top.title: Jeffery Simmons Sends Playful Warning To Tom Brady After Bears Win
top.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears kept their winning streak alive by beating the New Orleans Saints 21-13 on Sunday. This is the team’s fifth straight victory. Following the final whistle, defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons took time to speak with reporters on the field. He did not hold back when asked about the upcoming game against the Detroit Lions and the legendary quarterback watching from the booth. A Message for the Legend Simmons knows the buzz around Tom Brady is real, but he wants the Bears to stay focused on the job at hand. The defensive star told Fox Sports that the opponent in the booth changes nothing about their mindset. “It really don’t matter if it’s Detroit, Tom Brady — we’re still playing,” Simmons said. He made it clear that respect for Brady does not mean fear of the matchup. “No offense, much respect. The greatest quarterback to play this game, but it doesn’t matter who lines up across from us. Our job is to go out there and dominate,” he added. Simmons has faced Brady before during his time with the Tennessee Titans. When asked if he ever managed to sack the future Hall of Famer, Simmons laughed and admitted he could not recall a specific moment. Despite the lack of a sack, he noted that he did have a role in ending Brady’s season in New England. “I ended up putting him out of the playoffs his last year in New England, though, so that felt good,” he said. He also shared that former Titans coach Mike Vrabel has nothing but good things to say about the quarterback. Locker Room Bonds The playful tone Simmons showed on the field matches the energy inside the Bears’ locker room. Teammates are not afraid to mess with the defensive tackle during practice drills. Sports Mockery reported a specific incident involving defensive lineman Daniel Hardy. During a drill, the group had to tip the ball while a teammate tried to catch it. Hardy, knowing Simmons was standing behind him, decided to tip the ball far off course. Simmons had to scramble to catch the ball before it hit the turf. The defensive tackle showed his reaction with a single-finger salute afterward. Simmons believes Hardy did it on purpose to get a reaction. Hardy, however, maintains that the throw was wide and the whole thing was unintentional. This banter shows the team is comfortable with each other even as they fight for wins. Looking Ahead to Detroit The Bears will carry this momentum into their next game on the road. The team faces a tough test when they travel to Ford Field to play the Detroit Lions. This matchup will happen on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 p.m. ET. The Bears, coming off five straight wins, face the Lions.

top.title: Americas Football Round Up: Boca Juniors Crowned Copa Sudamericana Champions
top.description: This weekend had some monumental results across the Americas for football in 2026. The biggest headlines? Another international title for the famous Boca Juniors of Argentina, while the MLS and Liga MX playoffs took steps forward. Here is your recap of all the action. Boca Juniors Wins Copa Sudamericana Boca Juniors dominated the final of the 2026 Copa Sudamericana, emerging as 2-0 winners over Atletico Mineiro of Brazil. Santiago Ascacibar had the opener, and Miguel Merentiel had the dagger in the 48th minute as Boca won their third ever Sudamericana title, and their first since 2005. Boca had not won an international title in nearly two decades. Played in Colombia, Colombia’s own Sebastian Villa also contributed to the Boca victory, while Colombian international Alvaro Montero kept a clean sheet in goal, as they now chase another Argentine league title to close the season. Mineiro delivered a toothless performance as their focus now turns to the table finish in the Brasileiro. A match that was played in brutal heat and humidity, Boca’s leader, Argentine midfielder Leandro Paredes fainted post match during an interview with DSports the broadcaster. Flamengo Crowned Champions in Brazil Facing their direct rivals for the title Palmeiras, at the Palmeiras stadium, Flamengo did what they needed to do to win the 2026 Brazilian league title, a 1-1 draw with Palmeiras. Samuel Lino equalized the match in the 76th minute, to give Flamengo their 10th title. Palmeiras late season slump knocking them out of the title hunt before the season concludes. In an Easter Egg moment against a rival, Flamengo celebrated with the trophy in Palmeiras stadium, despite the CBF trying to prevent it, the 2025 League Champions Trophy was snuck into the stadium in an equipment bag, producing an iconic post-match scene. Flamengo, Palmeiras, and likely Cruzeiro have already punched their tickets to next year’s Copa Libertadores, and Palmeiras plays the Copa Libertadores 2026 final on Saturday against Estudiantes, meaning they can’t sulk from this draw for long. What hangs over the Brasileiro for 2027 and beyond is Brazil’s ban on sports betting and related advertising that is set to impact clubs financially. As for the rest of this season? Internacional, Gremio, and Corinthians are hovering on the relegation bubble, with Remo and Chapecoense already facing a grim fate. Sao Paulo and Botafogo are among the teams battling for a place in South American tournament football. Liga MX’s Liguilla is Set Monterrey’s 2-0 win over Pumas, via a brace from Argentine Luca Orellano that included a “bend it like Beckham” style goal from distance, was enough to secure their play in the final eight for the Liga MX playoffs to conclude 2026. Pumas were eliminated by other results around the league, and Monterrey were the team that survived despite playing with 10 men. Orellano is a talented player but he had adopted a bench role under Matias Almeyda, only to finish the regular season as a hero.

top.title: Davis Love III Defends Fanless RSM Finish After Weather Chaos
top.description: Davis Love III putts on eight during the first round of the U.S. Senior Open at Scioto Country Club in Columbus on July 2, 2026. Fans will not be present to view the final round as the PGA Tour season concludes. Davis Love III defended this controversial call after severe rain wiped out Saturday play at the RSM Classic. The tournament moved the decisive round to Monday, but the host said crowds cannot return due to a total loss of volunteer staff and security assets. Love admitted the scale of the storm caught everyone off guard. Speaking on Golf Channel during Sunday’s action, the Hall of Famer said, “We weren’t really prepared.” He noted that even the official Tour meteorologist on site did not expect such heavy rain. “Even our meteorologist on site from the Tour, they were surprised at what we got,” Love said. The downpour waterlogged the Seaside Course in Georgia, forcing officials to delay play multiple times until golf became impossible. Why Monday Crowds Are Impossible The logistics of a working Monday simply do not support a large fan base after such a disruption. Love stated that holding the final round before spectators on a working Monday is logistically unfeasible because vital infrastructure and manpower have been lost. The tournament lost access to its parking areas and, more critically, its 1,200 volunteers. “Parking, mainly our 1,200 volunteers. That’s the biggest thing,” he told GolfMagic . Without these people, the event cannot handle security, buses, or food services safely. Love emphasized that the players must still play to determine the winner and secure next year’s cards. “We’ve got guys playing not only to win a golf tournament but trying to improve their position and get a card for next year, and we can’t have fans because we’ve lost so many assets for tomorrow,” he added. A Season Ending in Silence This weather event has stripped the traditional Sunday atmosphere from the season’s conclusion. Despite MacCurrach Golf and Sea Island grounds staff executing an unbelievable job to drain the bunkers, the human element remains absent. Love acknowledged the trade-off, stating, “So we’re going to be able to get the players out to play, and that’s the main thing, give them a good golf course. Obviously they won’t hear quite as much cheering.” The players will finish the tournament in near silence. Refunds and exchanges for tickets purchased for Saturday remain subject to existing policies, meaning fans who paid for the washed-out action may not see the final round they bought. The weather disrupted the small tournament, which has limited resources. Love praised the bunkers for holding up well despite the rain events since they were built. “The bunkers performed very well,” he said. “MacCurrach Golf, the builder, did an unbelievable job building the bunkers, and we’ve had a lot of rain events since they were built and they held up really well.”

top.title: De Bruyne still 'loves' Man City owners despite financial charges
top.description: Kevin De Bruyne became one of Manchester City's all-time greats in a 10-year spell at the club (Paul ELLIS) Kevin De Bruyne said on Monday his love for Manchester City's leadership has not been tainted by a guilty verdict on breaking financial rules, that could tarnish his legacy at the English giants. Napoli playmaker De Bruyne returns to the Etihad Stadium in Champions League action on Tuesday, just over a year since his decade in Manchester came to an end. De Bruyne won six Premier League titles and the Champions League during a golden era for City to become one of the club's all-time greats. However, some of those titles could be stripped unless City successfully overturn a ruling that found them guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules between 2009 and 2018. "I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly, this is my club. I love the owners," De Bruyne told reporters. "I've even spoken to (chairman) Khaldoon (Al Mubarak) about how to buy a club. "I have nothing but affection for this club and that will never change, (the way) the people treated me and my family for 10 years." The Belgian also dismissed suggestions his achievements on the field are now tainted in light of City's financial impropriety. "In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit," he said. "I played in between the white lines. I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That's the thing that I value most." Napoli are in danger of an early Champions League exit after losing three of their opening four European games of the season. The Italians sit 27th in the 36-team table with only the top 24 progressing. City's form in the Premier League has slumped since their future in the English top-flight was plunged into doubt by the guilty verdict. A severe points deduction and possibly even relegation from the Premier League is expected if City's appeal is not upheld. top.title: NASCAR Finally Gives Fans The Horsepower Increase They Demanded
top.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR is finally listening to the fans who have begged for more speed. Beginning in 2027, the sanctioning body declared on Friday that horsepower will increase from 670 to 750 at intermediate-sized tracks. This change kicks off with the Coca-Cola 600 in May and affects major venues like Las Vegas, Kansas, and Michigan. The move addresses years of complaints about cars that were too slow to pass each other on these long ovals. At North Wilkesboro Speedway on May 23, the All-Star Race will see horsepower jump even higher to 800. This specific event will serve as a test bed. If the data looks good, NASCAR and engine builders could roll out this 800-horsepower package for all short tracks and road courses by mid-August at Bristol Motor Speedway. Speed Limits and New Rules NASCAR is also tweaking how drivers are penalized for going too low on the track. After a messy finish at Talladega last month, the rule book needed clarity. The new definition states that driving below the double-yellow line means a car’s left-side tires are “beneath the left line of the inside double-painted lines that separate the apron from the racing surface.” This removes the guesswork for drivers and officials alike. Superspeedways are getting their own adjustments for qualifying. Drivers will now have just one lap to set their time, ditching the old two-round format. Smaller spoilers and increased horsepower within the 510 to 530 range will also be featured during these sessions. NASCAR says these tweaks could push qualifying speeds past 200 mph. However, the race day rules at Daytona and Talladega will stay mostly the same as they were in 2026. Kevin Harvick has commented on the 2027 Clash setup modifications, noting NASCAR might eliminate the rear spoiler’s Lexan extension. Teams will also see the removal of splitter stuffers at every track next season. The removal of splitter stuffers at every track next season is expected to make the car react differently to various setups, forcing crews to find new ways to gain an edge. Rain rules are also shifting, as owner points will now decide the starting grid if qualifying gets washed out. The league is confident in its officials despite past controversies. A NASCAR executive stated, according to the Daily Downforce , “The Officiating Crew Is as Good as It Has Ever Been.” This comes as the sport removes minimum damper length rules to give teams more setup options.

This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. nigeria.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. nigeria.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

Despite competing in only nine tournaments during the 2026 season, Sinner recorded 44 wins in 47 matches, won six titles and reclaimed the world number one ranking during a 30-match winning streak. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitdeer Sells All 281 Bitcoin It Mined Last Week, Holds None Bitdeer sold every bitcoin it mined last week and still holds none of its own, the company said in its latest weekly update, continuing a nearly year-long strategy of turning production into cash after a weekend plunge in the bitcoin price. The Singapore-based miner reported output of 281.1 BTC and sales of 281.1 BTC for the week, for a net addition of zero. Its pure holdings, which exclude customer deposits, were zero as of Nov. 20. The sales came as bitcoin fell to a weekend low of $55,106 early Saturday at 1:17 AM ET, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The price has since bounced to near $62,700 as of 11:23 AM ET Monday. Bitdeer’s reserve has been drained all year Bitdeer’s treasury shrank from roughly 2,000 BTC at the end of 2025 to zero by Feb. 20, when Bitcoin Magazine reported the miner had liquidated its reserve over eight weeks. At the time, the company said the move should not be a concern for the broader market. Bitdeer’s filings show how little it has kept since. In its third-quarter results, filed with the SEC on a Form 6-K on Nov. 10, the company listed 47 BTC held at Sept. 30, down from 2,029 a year earlier. Its September production update showed 61 BTC held at the end of August. The company mined 1,355 BTC in September and 3,855 BTC in the third quarter, compared with 1,109 BTC in the same quarter of 2025. Self-mining margins stay thin Bitdeer has grown its fleet quickly. Self-mining hashrate reached 82.3 exahashes per second in the third quarter, up from 35.0 a year earlier, with another 28.7 exahashes per second of co-mining at third-party sites, the quarterly report shows . The economics are tight. Self-mining generated $217.5 million in revenue in the quarter but only $6.2 million in gross profit. Electricity averaged $47 per megawatt-hour, and the fleet ran at 15.4 joules per terahash. Bitdeer posted record revenue of $320.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $69.6 million, but a net loss of $125.5 million. That included a $54.6 million non-cash loss tied to a bitcoin-collateralized loan from a related party. Bitdeer also reported $213.7 million in cash and restricted cash, and its board authorized a new $100 million share repurchase program on Oct. 8. business.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. At 11.1 TH/s, the winning miner contributes about 0.000001% of that total, which fits Kolivas’s odds. One in 1,650 works out to a chance of about 0.06% over a full year of mining. Mining difficulty is about 134.8 trillion. The last adjustment cut it by about 9.1%, and the next one, expected around Nov. 26, is estimated to raise it by about 9.2%, according to mempool.space. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. sports.title: Where the Yankees' bullpen stands and what's next after latest addition
sports.description: Rebuilding the Yankees' bullpen was an early offseason priority for GM Brian Cashman. On Monday, the Yanks agreed with veteran lefty Brent Suter on a one-year contract, as first reported by ESPN's Jeff Passan. Suter, 37, an 11-year MLB veteran, split time last season with the Los Angeles Angels and Atlanta Braves, posting a 3.36 ERA (122 ERA-plus) in 54 appearances, covering 91 innings. Earlier this month, closer David Bednar accepted the $23.15 million free agent qualifying offer, securing his services for 2027. Veteran lefty Tim Hill was re-signed and the Yanks reunited with right-hander Jonathan Loaisiga on a two-year deal, after his successful 2026 season with the Arizona Diamondbacks . Right-handers Fernando Cruz and Luis Gil were non-tendered last week, saving roughly $4.6 million in estimated 2027 salary. The expensive reunion with Bednar and the signing of Loaisiga (set to earn $18 million through 2028) and Suter (guaranteed $4 million, with an option for 2028) might be the extent of the Yanks' heavy pursuit of relievers this winter. Top free agent lefty Adrian Morejon has the Yanks' interest, but he could command a lucrative multi-year deal, while free agent righty Paul Blackburn could net a similar contract as Loaisiga received. And the Yanks have further business to address - before or after the anticipated Dec. 1 MLB lockout - including ways to upgrade or boost depth at catcher, the infield and center field. Moving third baseman Ryan McMahon's remaining $16 million contract for 2027 and exploring potential deals for Luis Garcia Jr., Ryan Weathers and the Yanks' pitching surplus are also up for discussion. Suter gives the Yankees three lefties in their 2027 bullpen, along with Hill and Brent Headrick, a converted starter who had a breakout 2026 season but tired down the stretch. The soft-tossing Suter brings a wealth of bullpen experience and a knack for inducing soft contact and groundballs, which he did at a roughly 50-percent clip in 2026, per MLB Statcast. Armed with a sinker-changeup-fastball-slider mix, Suter has generally produced neutral splits; he was better against righty hitters in '26, limiting them to a .651 OPS versus .772 against lefty hitters. A 31st-round draft pick by the Milwaukee Brewers in 2012, Suter is a Harvard graduate who received his degree in environmental science and public policy. sports.description: Davis Love III putts on eight during the first round of the U.S. Senior Open at Scioto Country Club in Columbus on July 2, 2026. Fans will not be present to view the final round as the PGA Tour season concludes. Davis Love III defended this controversial call after severe rain wiped out Saturday play at the RSM Classic. The tournament moved the decisive round to Monday, but the host said crowds cannot return due to a total loss of volunteer staff and security assets. Love admitted the scale of the storm caught everyone off guard. Speaking on Golf Channel during Sunday’s action, the Hall of Famer said, “We weren’t really prepared.” He noted that even the official Tour meteorologist on site did not expect such heavy rain. “Even our meteorologist on site from the Tour, they were surprised at what we got,” Love said. The downpour waterlogged the Seaside Course in Georgia, forcing officials to delay play multiple times until golf became impossible. Why Monday Crowds Are Impossible The logistics of a working Monday simply do not support a large fan base after such a disruption. Love stated that holding the final round before spectators on a working Monday is logistically unfeasible because vital infrastructure and manpower have been lost. The tournament lost access to its parking areas and, more critically, its 1,200 volunteers. “Parking, mainly our 1,200 volunteers. That’s the biggest thing,” he told GolfMagic . Without these people, the event cannot handle security, buses, or food services safely. Love emphasized that the players must still play to determine the winner and secure next year’s cards. “We’ve got guys playing not only to win a golf tournament but trying to improve their position and get a card for next year, and we can’t have fans because we’ve lost so many assets for tomorrow,” he added. A Season Ending in Silence This weather event has stripped the traditional Sunday atmosphere from the season’s conclusion. Despite MacCurrach Golf and Sea Island grounds staff executing an unbelievable job to drain the bunkers, the human element remains absent. Love acknowledged the trade-off, stating, “So we’re going to be able to get the players out to play, and that’s the main thing, give them a good golf course. sports.description: Kyle McCord had a breakout preseason for the Green Bay Packers . It caught the attention of the Miami Dolphins, who traded for McCord at the end of training camp so he could be their backup quarterback behind former Packers QB Malik Willis. Now, he's getting a chance to start for the Dolphins. Though it's been a small sample size, starting in the regular season is proving to be much more of a challenge than those preseason games. Filling in the last two games for an injured Willis , McCord has completed only 44.6% of his passes, hasn't thrown a touchdown pass and is averaging only 4.8 yards per completion. Their 26-9 loss to the Super Bowl-contending Buffalo Bills on the road Nov. 22 was especially rough for McCord and the Dolphins. They had a season-low 185 yards of total offense and didn't find the end zone. McCord's 32.4 quarterback rating was the lowest of any quarterback in the NFL in Week 10. His 102 passing yards and 36.4 completion percentage – though his receivers had multiple drops – is also the lowest of all starting QBs. The Dolphins, who come to Lambeau Field to play the Packers on Dec. 20, dropped to 1-9. sports.title: NASCAR Finally Gives Fans The Horsepower Increase They Demanded
sports.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images NASCAR is finally listening to the fans who have begged for more speed. Beginning in 2027, the sanctioning body declared on Friday that horsepower will increase from 670 to 750 at intermediate-sized tracks. This change kicks off with the Coca-Cola 600 in May and affects major venues like Las Vegas, Kansas, and Michigan. The move addresses years of complaints about cars that were too slow to pass each other on these long ovals. At North Wilkesboro Speedway on May 23, the All-Star Race will see horsepower jump even higher to 800. This specific event will serve as a test bed. If the data looks good, NASCAR and engine builders could roll out this 800-horsepower package for all short tracks and road courses by mid-August at Bristol Motor Speedway. Speed Limits and New Rules NASCAR is also tweaking how drivers are penalized for going too low on the track. After a messy finish at Talladega last month, the rule book needed clarity. The new definition states that driving below the double-yellow line means a car’s left-side tires are “beneath the left line of the inside double-painted lines that separate the apron from the racing surface.” This removes the guesswork for drivers and officials alike. Superspeedways are getting their own adjustments for qualifying. Drivers will now have just one lap to set their time, ditching the old two-round format. Smaller spoilers and increased horsepower within the 510 to 530 range will also be featured during these sessions. NASCAR says these tweaks could push qualifying speeds past 200 mph. However, the race day rules at Daytona and Talladega will stay mostly the same as they were in 2026. Kevin Harvick has commented on the 2027 Clash setup modifications, noting NASCAR might eliminate the rear spoiler’s Lexan extension. Teams will also see the removal of splitter stuffers at every track next season. The removal of splitter stuffers at every track next season is expected to make the car react differently to various setups, forcing crews to find new ways to gain an edge. Rain rules are also shifting, as owner points will now decide the starting grid if qualifying gets washed out. The league is confident in its officials despite past controversies. A NASCAR executive stated, according to the Daily Downforce , “The Officiating Crew Is as Good as It Has Ever Been.” This comes as the sport removes minimum damper length rules to give teams more setup options.

technology.title: Bluetooth brakes are broken as researchers find anyone can control them
technology.description: Imagine something as mission-critical as the brakes on a trailer being vulnerable to unauthorized control. One Australian manufacturer made the interesting choice of building Bluetooth into a trailer brake controller without adequately securing its critical braking functions. Anyone within Bluetooth range of an unpatched Elecbrakes trailer controller could potentially trigger its brakes or apply more braking force than intended, without needing to authenticate. The discovery comes courtesy of a pair of security researchers from Element Digital, Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy. Their investigation began earlier this year when Forck was driving down the road and noticed that his physical Elecbrakes In-Car Remote had connected to someone else's trailer without pairing or prompting him. “It had connected mid-drive, without pairing or a prompt, to a brake controller that wasn’t mine, on a trailer I’d never seen, belonging to a driver who had no idea,” the researchers wrote . That one-off connection triggered a full-scale investigation by the pair. For those unfamiliar with trailer brake controllers, these devices are commonly used on larger trailers. Australian manufacturer Elecbrakes sells such controllers in Australia and New Zealand. Depending on jurisdiction, trailers over a certain weight are required to have their own braking system, which Elecbrakes manufactures. Elecbrakes offers two versions that are designed to be easier to install than traditional controllers: One that’s mounted in a vehicle, and one that is mounted directly on a trailer. That trailer-mounted unit can receive Bluetooth commands from the Elecbrakes smartphone app or a separate in-car remote. Given the importance of such control units to road safety, it’s easy to imagine how serious such a vulnerability could be if it proved to be easy to exploit, and boy, did it. Forck and McCarthy admitted they’re infrastructure security guys, not software devs, so they turned to Claude Code to dissect a decompiled copy of the Elecbrakes app, which Claude was happy to oblige. “What came back from the analysis was a map of the device’s entire Bluetooth GATT profile: 47 characteristics across four services, commands sent as plain unencrypted byte arrays, no checksums, no sequence numbers,” the researchers noted. To make matters worse, there was no authentication required for critical braking commands, even though other Bluetooth functions required pairing. Claude then built a web app that ran in Chrome which was able to access the Bluetooth controls for a nearby Elecbrakes system, and they were able to modify practically every aspect of brake control on a unit owned by one of them. Pairing failed on a few attempts, but not where it mattered: It allowed the connection without issue for actual brake control. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, is managing the acquisition, and NOAA will own and operate the instruments and deliver the data to users worldwide. The SMBA instruments could improve the medium-range forecasts for NOAA’s National Weather Service. The NEON mission is a collaboration between NASA and NOAA. The mission is led by NOAA, which provides funding, technical requirements, and postlaunch operations. NASA will manage the development of the NEON satellites and launch them for NOAA. science.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work

Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
science.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? science.title: NASA Seeks Partners to Design First Nuclear Reactor for the Moon
science.description: Artist’s concept of a nuclear fission power system on the Moon’s surface. Credit: NASA NASA is seeking industry partners to develop and test the first nuclear reactor designed to provide electricity on the Moon, a major step toward establishing a sustained human presence on the lunar surface. Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. Nuclear systems offer a reliable source of electricity in these challenging environments. LR-1 is managed by the agency’s Space Reactors Division in partnership with the Department of Energy. The division is also responsible for the development of NASA’s Space Reactor‑1 (SR-1) Freedom. Scheduled to launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom will deliver three SkyFall helicopters to Mars and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion, which uses electricity generated by a nuclear reactor to power spacecraft propulsion systems. science.description: null NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance rovers have spotted a bizarre assortment of Martian oddities, from potato chip-like rocks and ghostly white formations to mysterious patterns etched into the Red Planet's surface. While their appearances may be unusual, these formations offer scientists something far more valuable than a collection of curious snapshots: clues to the geological processes that shaped Mars over billions of years. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Some of the features are so thin and flat that the mission team likened them to potato chips, according to a statement from the space agency. NASA's Curiosity rover captured a close-up view of unusual, disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in Martian bedrock using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) on Nov. 7, 2026 (Sol 5067). The thin, flattened formations resemble tiny potato chips. The rover also used its ChemCam instrument to study the rocks' chemical composition, while samples from the Nazca drill site were delivered to its onboard Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) instrument for further analysis. Meanwhile, NASA's Perseverance rover has been investigating a collection of unusually bright rocks in an area called "Idubi," located in the “Lac de Charmes” region outside Jezero Crater. The rover captured images of the formations on Oct. 29, 2026 (Sol 2023), revealing pale, ghostly-looking rocks that stand out dramatically against the darker, dust-covered Martian landscape. Data from Perseverance's SuperCam instrument revealed that the rocks are rich in hydrated silica rather than being typical igneous rocks. That discovery has scientists particularly interested. On Earth, hydrated silica can form in environments involving hydrothermal activity or groundwater. These deposits are also capable of preserving microscopic fossils, making them valuable targets in the search for evidence of ancient life, according to another statement from NASA. science.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
science.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

science.description: A closing plenary session at the COP31 climate summit on 22 November AP Photo/Khalil Hamra/Alamy A deep rift among nations on how to tackle climate change, and whether the global economy can be weaned off fossil fuels, was exposed after the spectacular collapse of talks at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. They never were happy about it.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter The EU also took issue with a paragraph inserted at the behest of Saudi Arabia – which leads the 22-member Arab group of countries – calling for the rapid growth of carbon capture and storage technologies to the gigatonne scale by 2035. Carbon capture and storage technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and many sceptics are concerned that focusing on them will justify the continued use of fossil fuels and distract from the deep emissions cuts necessary for controlling climate change. Ireland’s climate minister Darragh O’ Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU, claimed the negotiations had been “hijacked by fossil fuel producers” and said the EU would “not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels”. science.title: What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars?
science.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. A model of one of the Phobos spacecraft on display in the Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics in Moscow, Russia. (Image credit: Музей Космонавтики from Россия, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons) To say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. Over the course of the next several weeks, Phobos 2 was able to overcome some of these setbacks and successfully began sending useful scientific data about the Martian environment back to Earth. By March, all the probe's science instruments appeared to be functioning normally, and despite the earlier loss of one of its processors, the remaining two had continued to facilitate control of the spacecraft by its Soviet ground control team. science.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
science.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. science.title: Ariane 6 rocket launching 36 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit on Nov. 24 after delay: Watch it live
science.description: null Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft is set for Tuesday morning (Nov. 24), and you can watch the action live. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Tuesday (Nov. 23), during a 29-minute window that opens at 5:45 a.m. EST (1045 GMT; 7:45 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. The launch was originally supposed to take place on Monday (Nov. 23), but that attempt was scrubbed due to a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace . Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. The upcoming mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.
